name: SIRTOM — Factorial HR software rollout
description: Internship at a public waste-management authority: I rolled out the Factorial HR software for all 67 staff, replacing paper and an Excel absence file, configured it to the authority's rules and drove adoption, including for field teams with little or no digital literacy.
context: SIRTOM de la région Flers-Condé is the public authority in charge of household waste collection and reduction for the Flers-Condé area, in Normandy. I was an intern at its head office from 13 May to 12 August 2024.

HR was run on paper, with an Excel file for absences. The authority had subscribed to Factorial, a cloud HR software, but nobody internally knew how to use it. My mission was to take it over, set it up for the way the authority actually works and get all 67 staff, across every department, using it.

Today, the authority describes Factorial's role in these terms: time tracking or schedules for around a hundred staff, rigorous tracking of leave and absences, a simpler approval path for requests, personal and shared documents available to every employee, and an information channel to staff, used for example for the professional elections of 10 December 2026.
The software was fully configured and in use three weeks before the end of my internship, which left time to follow its adoption and to work on other projects.

work.title: Taking over the software
work.text: I learned Factorial on my own, to the point where, as the authority's general director wrote in her recommendation letter, I knew it better than the vendor.

work.title: Full HR configuration
work.text: I moved every HR process that was on paper or in Excel into the software and set it up around the authority's own rules.
points: Time tracking (clock-in) and staff schedules.
Employment statuses: public-sector contract staff, fixed-term and permanent contracts, and more.
Payroll set-up in the software.
Absences and leave balances: paid leave, RTT days, recoverable hours, counter resets and leave carried over from one year to the next.
Organisation chart, approval chain and permissions, so each manager sees and validates only their own team.
HR documents stored in one place.

work.title: Fitting the tool to real constraints
work.text: The authority's reality did not match the software's defaults.
points: Many different employment statuses, each with its own leave and hour rules.
Collection crews working on a one-week-on, one-week-off schedule rotation, a pattern the software was not designed to handle.

My workaround for the rotation: Factorial lets you set a validity period on each schedule, so I created two schedules for these employees and made them alternate, each one active one week and inactive the next. I entered these alternating periods far into the future, up to the employees' likely retirement age (with a wide margin, since I chose not to ask anyone their age), so the rotation runs on its own with no manual changes.

work.title: Training 67 people with documentation
work.text: There was no time to train everyone one by one, so I wrote documentation per department, each team receiving only the parts that concerned it.

work.title: Visual and video guides for field teams
work.text: Part of the collection crews had very limited computer skills, and some had difficulty reading, which threatened both training and adoption. For them I replaced written guides with step-by-step visual and video tutorials: no need to read, just repeat the actions shown.

work.title: Adoption follow-up
work.text: After go-live, I followed adoption closely: answering many questions, training staff and convincing the most reluctant ones to switch.

work.title: Results
points: Several hours of HR work saved every week.
Fewer lost documents, and records much easier to find.
More accurate time tracking than the paper system, which was easy to get wrong or misuse.

note: No screenshots: the dashboards and documentation stay private, as they contain employees' personal data and internal processes.

name: ChauffeChauffe — CRM & ERP prototype
description: Team school project: a clickable CRM/ERP prototype for a heating maintenance company, built from a business case, when the assignment only asked for a feature plan and UI mock-ups.
context: ChauffeChauffe is a fictional family business repairing water heaters in Poitiers, used as a case study in class. The course material described a company running on paper: a customer complaint letter (a client left without heating for over a month), statements from the secretary and the technicians, and the paper service report slip they fill in after each call.

The assignment only asked for a theoretical deliverable: a plan of the features and of the user interface for a new internal tool. Our team decided to go further and build a working prototype that anyone can click through. It is a group project: the result is a team effort, not mine alone.

work.title: Diagnosis from the case
work.text: The documents pointed to a few root causes behind the client's month without heating.
points: Appointments managed in a paper planner, while technicians booked their own clients without telling the secretary.
Parts ordered only once the landlord had signed and posted back the invoice; delivered parts left unprocessed for two days; a second part forgotten.
No shared knowledge: each technician kept manuals and repair notes in his own way (personal folders, annotated paper manuals, memory), so the next technician arrived without the history.

work.title: Clients and scheduling
work.text: One record per client and a weekly calendar for the whole team.
points: Client file with address, equipment model and maintenance contract.
Weekly technician calendar showing each person's real constraints (finishes at 3:30 pm, recently hired, prefers distant jobs…) so the secretary can plan with them instead of around them.

work.title: Parts order pipeline
work.text: Every order is visible from approval to delivery, linked to its client and technician.
points: Four stages: awaiting approval, ordered, in transit, delivered.
Estimated delivery date on each order, so no part sits forgotten at the office.

work.title: Shared knowledge base
work.text: Manuals, procedures, safety notes and field tips per equipment model, written by the technicians and available to everyone, including new hires.

work.title: Billing (ERP)
work.text: Invoices tracked from draft to payment, with the split between tenant and owner.
points: Draft, sent, paid and cancelled statuses, totals invoiced, collected and pending.
Cost split between tenant and property owner, the step that blocked the repair in the case; CSV export.

work.title: What the prototype is
work.text: A clickable front end running on local demo data inspired by the case: it shows the experience and the data model, it is not connected to a real back end.
